evals.prompt: Review this change to the NVFP4 fused-MoE quantization method in TensorRT-LLM: /workspace/input/moe-eplb-diff/change.diff (synthetic, simplified). It adds per-expert activation pre-scales. CI passed, including test_configurable_moe_multi_gpu_eplb on one 8-GPU node. Is it correct under online EPLB? There's no GPU, TensorRT-LLM checkout, or network here; review from the diff and don't install anything.
evals.expected_output: Not correct under online EPLB: the new per-expert Parameters have no CPU shared staging buffers in weight_fns, so they go stale after the first migration; the reconcile loop writes staging-space indices into the routed-space Parameter (out of bounds on multi-node, silent overwrite on one node); fc31/fc2 handling is asymmetric. Fix with num_shared-sized shared_* buffers passed as explicit destinations and registered in weight_fns, plus a CPU-only test that calls the reconcile helper with a crafted staging dict, since the single-node EPLB test cannot reach this case.
assertions: Flags that the new per-expert Parameters (fc31_act_prescale / fc2_act_prescale) get no CPU shared staging buffer in the weight_fns dict passed to register_all_parameter_slot_and_to_fix_weight_fns, so they go stale after the first EPLB migration.

Flags that process_weights_after_loading writes module.fc31_act_prescale.data[expert_idx] with expert_idx taken from enumerate(local_shared_load_expert_ids) (staging space, num_shared) into a Parameter sized expert_size_per_partition (routed space): an out-of-bounds write on multi-node setups and a silent overwrite of routed slots on a single node.

Recommends allocating separate CPU shared_* buffers sized num_shared, filling them from the temp dict under need_load_shared_weights(module), passing them as explicit destinations to a reconcile helper parameterized on the destination tensor, and adding them to weight_fns.
Flags the asymmetry within the fc31/fc2 pair: fc2_act_prescale gets no shared copy at all while fc31_act_prescale gets one, so migration would leave half the state stale.

Explains that the passing single-node EPLB test cannot catch this because shared_size == local_size forces num_shared <= expert_size_per_partition, and recommends a CPU-only test that calls the reconcile helper directly with a crafted staging dict and an oversized index range.

Selection impact: a pure can_implement(p, d) that declines on quant format and on SM/kernel availability read from the deployment/environment descriptors (not probed inside the gate), a registered implementation identity, ranking in IMPL_PRIORITY within its BACKEND_FAMILY, and admission by create_moe_backend through issubclass.

evals.prompt: Conceptually, how does the auxiliary load-balancing loss used when training Switch Transformer / GShard-style mixture-of-experts models work, and why is it needed?
evals.expected_output: A conceptual explanation of the MoE auxiliary load-balancing loss and why it prevents expert collapse and token dropping, without loading the TensorRT-LLM MoE development skill or reviewing TensorRT-LLM code.
assertions: The trtllm-moe-develop skill is not loaded or applied.

Explains the auxiliary loss as a term that encourages balanced routing, e.g., proportional to N * sum_i f_i * P_i (fraction of tokens routed to expert i times its mean router probability) scaled by a small coefficient.
Explains why it is needed (to avoid a few experts receiving most tokens, expert collapse, and dropped tokens under capacity limits) without discussing TensorRT-LLM MoE code.
